2611.20981.title: Breaking feature collapse in self-supervised time series encoders
2611.20981.paper_summary: General-purpose time series encoders promise a single backbone that generalises across tasks and domains; however, they currently do not scale. We trace this down to a critical point of failure: under the predominant masked data modelling supervision, the encoder's output tokens partially collapse. This is the natural consequence of supervising encoders only in the input space, which leaves no constraint against redundant token dimensions in the feature space. We introduce OTISv2, which suppresses the collapse by complementing the reconstruction objective in input space with two objectives in the feature space: a self-distillation loss against an exponential-moving-average teacher, and a KoLeo regulariser. Under matched training, the resulting encoder reduces the cosine similarity and lifts the effective rank of its output tokens relative to its predecessor, and it scales monotonically from 7.1 M to 116 M parameters where its predecessor declines. It matches or surpasses existing general-purpose time series encoders across 143 uni- and multi-variate datasets. To foster further research, we release our code and pre-trained weights.
2611.20981.author: Özgün Turgut et.al.
